findings.explanation: The listed 'alert' conditions are only validity checks on link-speed variables (one repeated) and the filter string is truncated. The real logic: rolling 60-sample p95 of storage-network saturation percent against target_p95_pct (default 80), with critical at p95 >= 95 or repeated 90% bursts, high at p95 >= 90, warning at the target or a peak >= 95.
findings.quote: alert when `lkb` > 0, `elink` > 0, `denom_mbps` > 0, or `denom_mbps` > 0. Filter chain includes filter `(index=hci OR index=nutanix) sourcetype="nutanix:host:throug`.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the saturation calculation (controller bytes/s times 8 over negotiated link speed) and the four severity bands; drop the placeholder text.

findings.explanation: These Prism host stats metric names (dotted form), the use of controller I/O byte counters as 'CVM uplink' traffic against NIC link speed, and the TA sourcetypes `nutanix:cluster:metrics` / `nutanix:host` (the guide lists nutanix:cluster and nutanix:host, not :metrics) are unconfirmed; Prism metric names are often underscore-style, and storage I/O bandwidth is not necessarily the same as wire traffic on the NIC.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate the metric names against the Prism v2.0 stats documentation on a live cluster and explain why controller byte counters approximate uplink usage (or use NIC counters).

findings.explanation: The poller is described with a 30 second interval while implementation says one-minute sample alignment and the SPL comment assumes one-minute samples (window=60 is 'about one hour', window=3 'three minutes'); at 30 s the windows are half as long. The field named `peak_12` also takes a max over the 60-sample window.
findings.quote: ingest at a thirty second interval in the example below, a two to five minute time window
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one sample interval, state it, and set the window sizes and the peak field name accordingly.

findings.explanation: 'Cluster Viewer' is not a role name known from the grounding or standard Prism Element roles (Viewer, Cluster Admin, User Admin); the UI path 'Cluster, Network, CVM network' is also unconfirmed.
findings.quote: A Prism service account with Cluster Viewer on Prism Element
findings.suggested_fix: Check the exact read-only role and UI navigation in the Prism Element version you target.

findings.explanation: Splunkbase 5076 is not in the cached catalog, so the add-on name and ID cannot be confirmed from the repository data.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify on Splunkbase that 5076 is the Nutanix Prism add-on and that Splunk_TA_nutanix is its package name.

findings.explanation: Verified status is asserted for a design whose custom poller, REST metrics and add-on feeds are unconfirmed; there is no evidence of a lab run or SME sign-off beyond a team handle as reviewer.
findings.suggested_fix: Downgrade status until validated against a Prism Element cluster.

findings.explanation: Template text; the real causes (storage vMotion or live migration, resync after disk repair, backups, MTU or duplex errors) appear only in the troubleshooting section and are not given as false-positive scenarios.
findings.quote: Scheduled automation elevates `_time` without crossing `lkb` > 0 for UC-19.2.29.
findings.suggested_fix: Move those causes into knownFalsePositives with how to recognise each.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: `latest=@h` snaps the search window to the previous full hour, so a saturation event can take up to an hour to appear even though the alert is scheduled every 15 minutes; the leading backtick `comment(...)` macro is not built into Splunk.

summary: A good, clearly scoped bandwidth-axis use case with a plausible per-host SPL, but the description is template noise, the metric names and sample cadence are inconsistent, and several Nutanix and Prism facts are unconfirmed.
